AvellaMedinaDavisSamorodnitsky2025 proves oracle clipped-IPW quantile limits and only gives a parametric practical discussion, not a growing boundary-sieve feasible theorem.
No checked paper gives this escaping-compensator sharpness result for learned clipped-QTE weights.

novelty_flags.label: related_work and literature_checklist: AvellaMedinaDavisSamorodnitsky2025
novelty_flags.one_line: The core attributes the Lévy result to “Proposition 3.1,” but the inspected manuscript has Theorem 3.1 in Section 3 and the relevant finite-dimensional Lévy characterization in Proposition 8.2.

novelty_flags.label: Proposition 2 (sharp transfer)
novelty_flags.one_line: The escape witness refutes the internally proposed condition E_{a,n}=o_P(1), but names no published estimator or workflow that relies on that condition; present it as an intrinsic sharpness theorem or attach a concrete comparator.

soundness_flags.label: def:hall-class / def:drift-correction / def:quantile-estimator
soundness_flags.one_line: h_{a,n} and its empirical analogue are defined as exact solutions despite no existence convention, while the advertised feasible estimator uses oracle h_{a,n}, theta_a, and tail scores psi_{a,tau} requiring unknown q_a(tau); specify generalized inverses and a wholly data-driven threshold/score rule.

soundness_flags.label: honest_scope sanity reduction for thm:gaussian-branch
soundness_flags.one_line: Strict overlap is not a stated special case of P_S: its boundary link has alpha_a>0 and forces pi_a(x) to approach zero at the endpoint, so the claimed direct reduction to Firpo2007 fails.

soundness_flags.label: ass:hall
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited anchor assumes first-order regular variation, not the stated uniform second-order Hall expansion with a common remainder envelope; retag and justify it as a stronger rate condition or cite a source establishing that exact uniform class.

soundness_flags.label: ass:tail-marks
soundness_flags.one_line: The anchor supplies pointwise endpoint conditional-law convergence, not the stated common uniform convergence modulus over a model class; the stronger uniform condition needs a novel tag and justification or a supporting source.

soundness_flags.label: ass:conditional-density-modulus
soundness_flags.one_line: The anchor’s stated condition is endpoint conditional anti-concentration, not a common conditional-density continuity modulus; align the condition with the source or justify the stronger uniform density requirement.

soundness_flags.label: ass:boundary-multiplier and ass:holder
soundness_flags.one_line: Membership in a fixed Hölder ball includes a uniform sup-norm bound for g_a, which already yields fixed positive upper and lower bounds for exp(g_a); ass:boundary-multiplier is redundant as written.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 3–6, Assumption 2.2 and equations (7)–(12); p. 6, Theorem 3.1; pp. 20–21, Propositions 8.1–8.2; pp. 12–13, Section 6; pp. 41–42, Section 8.7
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper states first-order regular variation, endpoint conditional-law convergence, and conditional anti-concentration; Theorem 3.1 is the fixed-quantile oracle limit, Proposition 8.2 supplies its finite-dimensional Lévy characterization, Section 6 discusses only a well-specified parametric propensity fit, and Section 8.7 says full subsampling consistency requires further development.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record, pp. 1161–1189
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article studies efficient ATE estimation using a nonparametrically estimated propensity score, not quantile estimation or a weak-overlap Hall-boundary result.
Firpo develops a two-step nonparametric-propensity QTE estimator with root-n consistency, asymptotic normality, and semiparametric efficiency under the regular setting.
The paper gives irregular-IPW and doubly robust limit theory and an adaptive m-out-of-n bootstrap for causal parameters with alpha-stable limits.
Dorn studies thresholded doubly robust ATE inference under weak overlap with nonparametric nuisance estimation, rather than a quantile convex-argmin or boundary-chart likelihood theorem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Make the estimator genuinely implementable: replace both tail-normalization equations by generalized-inverse conventions, select clipping from fitted-propensity order statistics or a specified data-driven grid, and use a preliminary quantile in the endpoint score estimate.

Retag the uniform second-order Hall, endpoint-modulus, and conditional-density-modulus conditions as novel uniformity assumptions, then give a concise member-family argument showing why they hold on the proposed boundary chart.

Repair the sharp-transfer comparison by naming a published learned-weight rule whose usual relative-consistency rationale fails, or recast the proposition as a companion mathematical sharpness result without diagnostic language.
Add a local minimax lower bound for the signed boundary likelihood functional to turn the displayed feasible rate into a matched frontier rather than only an achievability mechanism.

recommended_next_step: Revise the implementable construction, correct the Avella-Medina proposition citation and sanity reduction, and regularize the strengthened uniform assumptions before advancing to Stage 0.
